items.title: Section: Tainted and Untainted Craving, Three Ways Affliction Actually Ceases

items.zh: 當知此愛是染污愛。若有起心，專求離欲，欣樂證入上地寂靜，當知此愛是不染污。復有三種諸法斷滅。謂對治斷滅、現行斷滅、棄捨斷滅。諸煩惱事之所顯現，是初斷滅。諸行生滅之所顯現，是第二斷滅。若生上地，或入無餘依涅槃界，下地諸行及一切行棄捨所顯，是第三斷滅。
items.en: One should know this craving is tainted craving. If a mind arises that single-mindedly seeks freedom from desire, delighting in entering the higher realm's own stillness, one should know this craving is untainted. There are also three kinds of cessation of defiled states: cessation through antidote, cessation through non-manifestation, and cessation through abandonment. What is manifested through the non-arising of afflictive grounds is the first cessation. What is manifested through the arising and passing of formations is the second cessation. What is manifested through the abandonment of lower-realm formations, or of all formations, upon rebirth in a higher realm or entry into nirvana without residue, is the third cessation.

items.title: Section: Three Ways a Practitioner Falls Back

items.zh: 復有三退。一、未得法退，二、已得法退，三、習行法退。
items.en: There are also three kinds of falling back: falling back from what has not yet been attained, falling back from what has already been attained, and falling back in habitual practice.

items.title: Section: Three Paths Within the Threshold of Absorption

items.zh: 復依世間諸近分定，若方便道、若無間道、若解脫道，或為斷滅、或為證得而修習者，彼於所緣或觀過失、或觀寂靜，觀下過失，觀上寂靜。
items.en: Depending further on the various worldly threshold concentrations, whether the preparatory path, the uninterrupted path, or the liberation path, and whether cultivated in order to cut off affliction or in order to actually attain the higher absorption, the practitioner's object is either contemplating faults or contemplating stillness, contemplating the lower realm's own faults or the higher realm's own stillness accordingly.

items.title: Section: Six Mental Applications Complete the Threshold of Absorption

items.zh: 若勝進道，當知彼是遍滿所緣、或無漏緣。復次，諸近分攝六種作意，謂了相等，乃至加行究竟作意。此中了相、勝解作意，方便道攝；遠離、加行究竟作意，無間道攝；攝樂作意，四種道攝；觀察作意，勝進道攝。
items.en: The path of continued advancement takes as its object either the pervasive object or the uncontaminated object. Each threshold concentration further contains six kinds of mental application: understanding the signs and so on, through the application-perfecting attention. Among these, understanding the signs and resolute understanding belong to the preparatory path; withdrawal and the application-perfecting attention belong to the uninterrupted path; gathering joy belongs to all four paths; and observation belongs to the path of continued advancement.

items.title: Section: Why Concentration Cannot Be Grasped by Thought Alone, and Two Magicians Whose Powers Collide

items.zh: 問：何緣故說修靜慮者靜慮境界不可思議？答：修靜慮者已善修治磨瑩其心，有如是相威德勢力，隨所欲為皆能成辦，非不如意，法性故爾。是故說彼由尋思道不可思議。復有二種修靜慮者，於一事中俱發變事勝解神通皆得自在，此二神通互相障礙，而此二通無偏大者不相映奪。彼後無間，一於此事神通無礙，如其所欲皆能轉變，第二神通便被障礙。此中因緣云何應知？由彼二人勢力威德皆悉平等，俱時發起變現神通，然其所作互不相似。由彼神通所欲為事不相似故，於此一事二種神通互相障礙。爾時有一，作是思惟：何因緣故我此神通今有障礙，將無我定有退失耶？此一定者，即於此事起是餘心。第二定者，即於此事數數專注心無散亂，所發神通能無障礙，隨神通力如意轉變。若二神通威德不等，隨其勝者所作成辦；若二神通威德相似，先作意者成辦非餘。
items.en: Question: Why is it said that the absorption-state of a meditator is inconceivable? Answer: A meditator who has thoroughly cultivated and polished the mind possesses such majesty and power that whatever is wished can be accomplished, never falling short, this being simply the nature of the dharma. Therefore it is said that this cannot be grasped through the path of reasoning. If the power of two miraculous abilities is unequal, the more powerful one prevails; if the two are equal, whichever one applied intention first prevails, not the other.

items.title: Section: Four Kinds of Meditator, and the Four Ways Craving, View, Pride, and Doubt Taint Absorption

items.zh: 復有四種修靜慮者。一、依近分定修靜慮者。二、依染污定修靜慮者。三、依世間定修靜慮者。四、依出世間定修靜慮者。於六作意，謂了相等，乃至加行究竟作意修定轉時，當知是初。愛上靜慮，廣說乃至疑上靜慮，當知第二。
items.en: There are also four kinds of person who cultivate absorption: one who cultivates by way of threshold concentration, one who cultivates by way of tainted concentration, one who cultivates by way of worldly concentration, and one who cultivates by way of transcendent concentration. Craving-tainted absorption, extensively explained through doubt-tainted absorption, is the second kind.

items.title: Section: Worldly Absorption, Transcendent Absorption, and the Absorption Without Perception

items.zh: 若住餘善世間靜慮，當知第三。謂能引發現法樂住無量作意世間功德，又能引發遊戲神通。若順決擇分所攝受空、無願、無相解脫門所顯靜慮，當知第四。復次，無想等至，當言唯一有漏。
items.en: If one dwells in a wholesome worldly absorption otherwise free of taint, this is the third kind, able to draw forth present-life abiding in bliss and the immeasurable states of mind as worldly excellent qualities, as well as playful miraculous powers. If the absorption is manifested by the liberation gates of emptiness, wishlessness, and signlessness that are embraced by what is conducive to penetration, this is the fourth kind. The attainment without perception, furthermore, should be said to be exclusively contaminated.

items.title: Section: The Cessation of Feeling and Perception — Uncontaminated, Transcendent, Reserved Even by Bodhisattvas

items.zh: 滅盡等至當言無漏。由與煩惱不相應故、非相應故、無所緣故、非諸煩惱之所生故。是出世間，一切異生不能行故。唯除已入遠地菩薩。菩薩雖能起出世法，令現在前，然由方便善巧力故，不捨煩惱。又此等至，當言非學非無學攝，非所行故，似涅槃故。
items.en: The attainment of cessation should be said to be uncontaminated, being unassociated with affliction, being without any associated mind or mental factors, being without object, and not being produced by affliction. It is transcendent, since no ordinary being is able to practise it. The sole exception is a bodhisattva who has already entered the far-going ground. Though a bodhisattva can manifest this transcendent state, through the power of skilful means affliction is not abandoned. This attainment should be said to belong to neither the trainee's path nor the adept's, since it is not what either practices, and it resembles nirvana.

items.title: Section: Four Sutras Cited in Turn, Beginning with Mindfulness Carried with the Body

items.zh: 復次，當釋隨身念經。謂心清淨行苾芻，有四種隨煩惱。一、毀犯禁戒，二、散亂尋思，三、保著內身，四、保著外境。毀禁戒者，由憂悔門，於三摩地能為障礙。亂尋思者，由三種門。一、由於過去境隨念散亂門；二、由依掉舉、流散、惡見、惡聞、惡語、惡行，唯樂聞思散亂門；三、由先串習勢力所持散亂門。
items.en: The Sutra of Mindfulness Carried with the Body shall now be explained. A monk practising purity of mind has four secondary afflictions: transgressing the precepts, scattered deliberation, clinging to the inner body, and clinging to outer objects. Transgressing the precepts obstructs concentration through the gateway of worry and regret. Scattered deliberation arises through three gateways: the gateway of scattering through recollecting past objects; the gateway of scattering through restlessness, distraction, wrong view, and delighting only in hearing and thinking; and the gateway of scattering sustained by the force of prior habituation. Clinging to the inner body arises through the gateway of finding no weariness with birth and death.

blocks.text: How afflictions are stilled, how practitioners fall back, and the attainment of cessation, which only noble ones can reach.

Master Cháng Bǎi: a practitioner should meditate in order to leave desire, not for love of meditative joy. Affliction ceases by antidote, by not manifesting, or by rebirth above; an ordinary person reborn above gives up lower formations only for a time and will return.
From what is not yet attained, and from what is attained.
Master Cháng Bǎi: application before root absorption; cutting the hindrances; release. One enters meditation by disgust for the lower as coarse and delight in the higher as fine.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the sphere of concentration cannot be known by reasoning; it must be realised. Of two magicians with equal power, the one who intends first succeeds.
Master Cháng Bǎi: absorptions tainted by craving, views, pride, and doubt belong to one who meditates in a tainted way.

Master Cháng Bǎi: after non-perception, one returns to the three realms; cessation resembles nirvāṇa. No ordinary being can enter cessation. Bodhisattvas keep the afflictions cut by cultivation, to take birth and save beings.
Master Cháng Bǎi: some cherish and protect their own body too much and cannot bear hardship. Some only enjoy hearing and thinking about the Dharma and never meditate.
"It cannot be known by reasoning; it must be realised." The treatise describes meditation in words while reminding us that words are not the point.

quiz.q: What kind of craving is untainted?
options: a mind single-mindedly seeking freedom from desire, delighting in entering the higher realm's stillness
loving the joy of meditation and wishing for lasting rebirth among the gods
loving worldly fame and gain
loving friends and family
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: a practitioner should meditate in order to leave desire, not out of love for meditation's joy or for rebirth among the meditative gods. So aspiration is judged by what it seeks. The tainted kind's detail is missing from the English.

quiz.q: What are the names of the three kinds of cessation?
options: cessation with residue, without residue, and by the nature of things
cessation through antidote, through non-manifestation, and through abandonment
cessation by seeing, by cultivation, and by no-more-learning
cessation by precepts, by meditation, and by wisdom
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: what is shown by afflictions no longer arising is the first, cessation through antidote; making afflicted formations temporarily not manifest is the second. The lecture offers several further schemes, so this question asks only for the names.

quiz.q: In cessation through abandonment, how do an ordinary person and a third-fruit sage differ when born higher?
options: no difference: both abandon them forever, since seeds fade on birth above
the ordinary person forever, the sage for a time
the ordinary person abandons them only for a time and returns; the sage abandons them for good
both must return to be born below
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: an ordinary person reborn above can only temporarily give up the lower formations, and since the seeds of affliction are not cut, will come back below. A third-fruit sage reborn above gives them up forever.

quiz.q: Per Master Cháng Bǎi, what are the preparatory and uninterrupted paths in worldly threshold concentration?
options: the preparatory path follows root absorption, and the uninterrupted path is the rest after it
both are transcendent paths belonging to sages only
the preparatory path is application before root absorption, and the uninterrupted path is cutting the hindrances
both are other names for the liberation path
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: while in application and not yet in root absorption is the preparatory path; while cutting the hindrances that block absorption is the uninterrupted path. Being freed and attaining root absorption belongs to the liberation path. Each is a stage in worldly practice.

quiz.q: How does one practising worldly threshold concentration contemplate the object?
options: contemplating lower stillness and higher faults, knowing the dangers above
contemplating impermanence alone, with no distinction of levels
contemplating suchness alone, with no concrete objects
contemplating the lower realm's faults and the higher realm's stillness
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: relying on disgust for the lower as painful, coarse, and obstructed, and delight in the higher as pure, fine, and free, one enters meditation. This method of disliking below and delighting above marks the worldly path.

quiz.q: Which of the six mental applications belongs to all four paths?
options: observation, every path requiring constant examination, as the text assigns
gathering joy
understanding the signs
withdrawal
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: practising gladly through gathering joy belongs to the preparatory path; cutting middle-grade afflictions, the uninterrupted; attaining their cessation, the liberation path; and advancing further, the path of advancement. Observation belongs to advancement alone.

quiz.q: To which kind of meditator do craving-tainted through doubt-tainted absorption belong?
options: the one by way of threshold concentration, as not yet in root absorption
the one who cultivates by way of tainted concentration
the one by way of worldly concentration
the one by way of transcendent concentration
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: absorptions tainted by craving, views, pride, and doubt are the second kind, one who meditates by way of tainted concentration. The explanation of the first kind is missing from the English, so only the second is tested.

quiz.q: This is rendered "embraced by the liberation gates ... belonging to decisive discernment." What is wrong?
options: nothing: the gates belong to this very Section on Decisive Discernment, as the lecture has it
空 should be "sky"
解脫門 is left out
the structure is reversed, as the 順決擇分 stage embraces the gates, which reveal the absorption; 順 is lost too
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the stage conducive to penetration is still with outflow, and the gates of emptiness and the rest come with seeing. Through that stage the gates exist. The English drops 順 and reuses the name of this Section, inviting confusion.

quiz.q: §21 has "with outflow" for 有漏, and §22 "undefiled" for 無漏. What is the issue in wording?
options: 有漏 and 無漏 are a pair, yet the English pair is lost, and "undefiled" sits close to "untainted"
none: the two are not a pair, so different wording is needed, as the lecture distinguishes, so nothing needs changing
they should be "bound" and "unbound"
both should simply be "absorption"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: after emerging from non-perception one still returns to the three realms; cessation resembles nirvana. §15 uses "untainted" for wholesome craving in the desire realm, so "undefiled" and "untainted" are too close while meaning different things.

quiz.q: This is rendered "being unassociated with affliction, being unassociated." What is the problem?
options: none: the treatise repeats itself for emphasis, and the lecture sees no difference
"affliction" should be deleted
the two read as a repetition, though 《披尋記》 has freedom from craving and then the ceasing of mental states
it should be "being associated"
quiz.why: The 《披尋記》 quoted in the lecture distinguishes them: the first is having left craving for the highest spheres, the second is the ceasing of mental states. Master Cháng Bǎi explains the second accordingly. The English loses the distinction.

quiz.q: A bodhisattva can enter cessation yet does not abandon affliction. How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain this?
options: they keep the afflictions of the path of cultivation, retaining them to take birth and save beings in the three realms
they are too weak to cut afflictions, and are thus inferior to arhats
they have no afflictions left to abandon
they never enter cessation
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: they do not give up the afflictions of cultivation, keeping them to take birth and save beings. A seventh-ground bodhisattva can enter cessation without fully cutting afflictions. The treatise credits this to skilful means, not to weakness.

quiz.q: Which four secondary afflictions does a monk practising purity of mind have?
options: desire, hatred, dullness, and restlessness, the first four hindrances
flattery, deceit, pretence, and deception
arrogance, unwillingness, disbelief, confusion
transgressing the precepts, scattered deliberation, clinging to the inner body, clinging to outer objects
quiz.why: These four are specific to this sutra. Master Cháng Bǎi on the third: one especially cherishes and protects one's own body, cannot bear hardship and strive, and thus obstructs meditation. Options C and D come from other lists.
